title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-28
lineage: Master Reel (Teac A-6100) -> Advent Advocate Dolby B Unit -> Fostex FR-2LE -> WAV (24bit/96k)  Mastering Info: WAV -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC/16
source: SBD -> Shure Line Mixers -> Advent Advocate Dolby B Unit -> Master Reel (Sony Deck - BASF Tapes - 1/4 Track - 7 1/2 ips)

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show with smoking Hard To Handle, Morning Dew and Dark Star, plus crystal‑clear organ and drums
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced soundboard delivers exceptionally clear audio that showcases Ron’s organ, Jerry’s soaring guitar tone and Bill’s killer drum solo, despite a few minor tape‑speed quirks. Musically the concert is a fire‑starter – Hard To Handle, Morning Dew, Bird Song and an expansive Dark Star/Other One suite are repeatedly singled out as definitive performances, while only Playin’ suffers noticeable flubs.

ai_rating.rationale: Out of 18 reviews the average rating is ~4.9 stars; the vast majority praise both performance and sound quality, with only a couple of modest critiques.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix that reveals subtle flaws (minor tape‑speed irregularities, occasional level dip on Hard To Handle) but overall delivers a clear, balanced listening experience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set fires up with tight, uptempo numbers and a soaring Dew; second set moves into more cerebral, introspective territory culminating in an epic Dark Star/Other One suite.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for perfect tone, prime form, occasional out‑of‑tune moments noted but overall stellar guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as laying down ‘bombs’ and picked harmonics; solid bass foundation throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for a standout solo on Hard To Handle and inspired fills on Bertha.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron’s organ is loud, clear and “perfect”; Tom Constanten’s texture mentioned in the Dark Star mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drum solo called ‘ridiculously killer’; overall drumming praised as tight and powerful.
